issues.body: The mutation boundary calls `_live_hold` for the PR issue and source issue, but never re-fetches `repos/{repo}/pulls/{number}` or compares its current head SHA and worker ref with the earlier `head_sha`/`issue_number`. All authorization inputs, receipt recognition, verdict selection, episode construction, and the comment marker remain bound to the earlier head. A force-push between the initial pull read and the first write can therefore cause labels and a receipt for the old SHA to be applied while the PR now points at a different head.
issues.fix_hint: Immediately before the first possible write, re-fetch the pull request and require exact equality of the current head SHA and relevant head ref/source-issue binding with the values used for adjudication. Stand down mutation-free on mismatch. Add an end-to-end non-vacuous test that changes the head between planning and the boundary and asserts that no comment or label write occurs.
issues.title: The mutation boundary still is not bound to the current pull request head

issues.body: `in_flight` is computed once from the initial `timeline` and copied into `probe`; the boundary then calls `admission(..., **probe)` unchanged. `_live_hold` fetches a new timeline only to answer machine ownership and does not return the newest live hold application time or fresh receipt/comment evidence. If the original hold is removed and machine-reapplied after the receipt during the API gap, ownership can still be machine-owned while stale `readmission_in_flight=True` bypasses the cap for what is now a new park.
issues.fix_hint: At the mutation boundary, fetch the fresh timeline and relevant bot comments/receipts, recompute `newest_label_application`, `recorded_loop`, receipt stamps, and `incomplete_readmission`, and pass that fresh result to `admission`. Add a test that moves the live hold application from before to after the receipt between planning and mutation and asserts `readmissions-spent` with zero writes.
issues.title: The mutation boundary still reuses stale final-slot hold-ordering evidence

verdict.summary: Both round-3 trust-boundary findings remain in the submitted diff. The new helpers and self-tests describe fresh head and hold-ordering requirements, but the live mutation path still rechecks only labels and ownership. It neither re-fetches the pull request head before writing nor recomputes the final-slot in-flight proof from the fresh timeline. Consequently, a force-push can receive mutations authorized for the prior head, and a newly reapplied hold can inherit the stale cap exception. Progress is stagnant because the same blocker and major issue remain at the same severities.
